extracted.intended_audience: science policy researchers, grant program officers, scholars of peer review, and policymakers interested in U.S. research funding
extracted.subtask_description: Schema of evaluative dimensions and reform topics for peer review as applied to U.S. science policy and grant-making, covering cultural axioms, procedural practices, bibliometric and qualitative evaluation, misconduct, conflicts of interest, and reform pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Centrality of Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is treated as a central family of quality-control mechanisms for U.S. science policy and the functioning of research systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers both symbolic and practical value; framing criterion for judging the legitimacy and role of peer review in policy and funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Is "Peer Review"?
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and boundaries of peer review as a concept — what activities and processes are included under the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for delimiting evaluation scope (journal refereeing, grant panels, program reviews) and for comparing different forms of peer assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Axioms about the Culture of Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundational assumptions or cultural principles that shape how peer review is practiced and interpreted within scientific communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These axioms function as normative touchstones when assessing peer review's fit with disciplinary norms and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Evaluating Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit dimensions and standards used to judge the quality, fairness, and effectiveness of peer-review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section title implies an enumerated set of evaluative criteria (procedural fairness, expertise matching, transparency, reliability, validity, timeliness); the book explores these dimensions in depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review at Major Agencies (NIH, NSF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency-specific practices and standards for proposal review as implemented at NIH and NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative criteria include panel composition, scoring systems, award rate metrics, and agency-specific procedures; useful when evaluating agency grant-review fidelity and differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trends in Proposal Volume and Award Rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical metrics tracking application pressure and success rates as indicators of funding system performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess competitiveness, gatekeeping effects, and potential systemic stressors on peer review (e.g., growing volume, falling award rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical Studies of Grants Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological standards and evidence used to study the operation and outcomes of grants peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses agency-sponsored, independent, and survey-based studies — relevant for judging the evidentiary basis of claims about peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success in the Pursuit of Research Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes-based criterion: who wins funding, patterns of success and failure and their explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines correlates of funding success (track records, institutional affiliation, topic fit) and consequences for careers and research agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Consequences of Failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation dimension addressing the downstream effects on researchers and the research enterprise when proposals are rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers demoralization, career impacts, resubmission dynamics, and systemic loss of lines of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition for Research Support / Upward Creep and Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and behavioral criteria: how competition shapes proposal inflation, repeated resubmissions, and strategic behaviour by applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to judge whether peer review produces perverse incentives that distort research proposals and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inferences: Peer Review and Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for identifying, managing, and evaluating the impact of conflicts of interest on review outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses both perceived and actual conflicts and their implications for fairness and legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Purposes of Scientific Publication and Journal Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for judging journal peer review in light of the goals of scientific publishing (quality control, dissemination, priority, credibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for comparing grant-review aims with journal-review aims and for assessing whether practices serve stated purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles and Practices: The Tensions of Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Normative dimensions that capture tensions between ideals (objectivity, meritocracy) and operational practices (biases, gatekeeping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps evaluate whether specific peer-review arrangements balance principles appropriately or create systemic contradictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Practices / An Analysis of Referee Commentary / The Rhetoric of Referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for assessing the content, tone, usefulness, and rhetorical features of referee reports and editorial correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes analytic attention to specificity of critique, constructive guidance vs. gatekeeping rhetoric, and evidence-based commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Malpractice Defined / Fraud and Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for defining scientific malpractice and assessing whether peer review can detect or deter misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers the limits of peer review in identifying fraud, the social dynamics of scapegoating, and institutional responses to allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Augmenting Peer Review: The Place of Research Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatives and supplements to conventional peer review for assessing research quality (evaluation frameworks beyond blind panel review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces the role of program evaluation, expert assessment, and hybrid models as criteria for improving decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliometrics as Research Evaluation: The Promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of citation-based and other bibliometric indicators as evaluative metrics for research and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses generations of bibliometrics, their promises and limits, and when they are (or are not) appropriate supplements to peer judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converging Partial Indicators / Evaluative Bibliometrics and Beyond
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion emphasizing the use of multiple, partial indicators combined to assess research performance more robustly than any single metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports composite or convergent-evidence approaches and cautions about overreliance on single proxies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative Scientometrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of qualitative methods (case studies, expert narratives) as legitimate evaluative inputs alongside quantitative metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues for integrating qualitative assessment to capture dimensions that bibliometrics miss (novelty, interdisciplinarity, societal relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges and New Directions / Impediments and Nagging Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of persistent problems and barriers that any evaluation or reform must address (institutional inertia, resource limits, political pressures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a checklist of obstacles to successful evaluation/reform efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reforming Peer Review: Changing Roles, Rules, and Toward a Process of Reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Process-oriented criteria for designing and implementing reforms to peer-review systems, including governance, transparency, and role changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes modest incremental changes from more iconoclastic reforms, and emphasizes process design for durable improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-Analysis, The Science Critic, and Science Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for synthesizing evidence across studies (meta-analysis) and for the role of critical scholarship in informing policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights methodological rigor in aggregating results and the normative role of critics in shaping policy reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy Research and the Public Interest / Science Policy and the Flywheel of Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria linking peer-review practice to broader public-interest objectives of science policy and the systemic dynamics that sustain or impede desired outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess whether peer-review arrangements align with democratic accountability, societal needs, and long-term health of the research ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventing Tools for Perception and Foresight
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative dimension emphasizing development of tools (indicators, foresight methods) to improve perception of emerging needs and to anticipate consequences of funding choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages designing forward-looking metrics and analytic tools as part of a comprehensive evaluation strategy.
